findings.failure_path: The new later-peer precedence heuristic checks authority level but not whether later text is an instruction at all. Instructions embedded in a candidate diff, retrieved document, or tool output can appear later within the same user/tool context and be treated as peers, allowing prompt-injection data to override an earlier legitimate instruction without crossing a formal authority boundary.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit positional precedence to genuine instructions at the same authority and trust level, explicitly state that quoted or untrusted data never gains authority from position, and add a same-role embedded-instruction probe.

findings.failure_path: The rewrite retires the explicit obligation that attention limitations never excuse a violated rule, while the bounded candidate contains no semantic-control zero-loss map required by the unchanged rule at line 164. An agent can now cite finite attention or constraint count to excuse violating a loaded same-authority safety or contract rule; the narrower statement that this is not a reason to refuse adding a rule does not prevent that behavior.
findings.smallest_fix: Restore a concise no-excuse sentence and add the required semantic-control evidence row mapping every predecessor obligation to surviving or genuinely subsuming text.

findings.failure_path: The candidate says the behavioral probe graded final text with no grading standard, while this added rule requires the grading standard to precede the change or come from a party blind to the candidate. Consequently the claimed 10/10 deletion-safety result is post-hoc evidence and cannot establish that the high-risk boundary is contained.
findings.smallest_fix: Freeze an objective rubric before rerunning extracted version-control arms, or use a candidate-blind grader; retain prompts, raw outputs, repeated-run spread, and the predetermined verdict logic in the evidence record.

concern_results.conclusion: The revised precedence rule is incomplete: it protects authority boundaries but does not distinguish genuine instructions from later untrusted data.
A later prompt embedded in a diff, document, or tool output could be misclassified as a same-authority peer and incorrectly receive precedence.
The supplied evidence exercises lower-authority conflicts only; it does not cover the same-role untrusted-data bypass or demonstrate recovery from misclassification.
The reported probe was designed against final text with no predeclared grading standard, contradicting the new measurement rule and leaving no valid release-grade evidence.
The rewrite drops the prior explicit rule that attention limitations never excuse a violated requirement, weakening behavior for same-authority contract conflicts.
No required semantic-control zero-loss obligation map is present for this shared-skill rule retirement, so safe rollout or restoration of removed obligations is unsupported.
Only aggregate success counts are supplied; prompts, arm provenance, grading decisions, and raw failures are absent, preventing diagnosis or reproduction.
The authority-boundary protection does not contain the adjacent trust-boundary bypass, and its deletion-safety evidence is invalid under the candidate's own preregistration standard.
